symptom: patch passes visible and hidden checks on both pandas versions but the differential check diverges on probe [[], ["t1","a"]] (expected [["t1","a",1]])
root_cause: patch replaced pd.DataFrame(records, columns=[...]) with a manual loop over records; the loop raises ValueError/IndexError on a record shorter than two elements, while DataFrame pads the short row with NaN and value_counts drops it
validity: synthetic case derived from release notes; padding and drop verified on pandas 3.0.3 only; 2.3.3 behavior inferred from the golden output; divergence with this probe seen in 5 of 10 p4 effort=low runs (spark-1.3 and wonder-1.0, n=5 each)
lesson: Replacing a library call with a hand-written loop can silently drop implicit behavior (here short-row handling) that no visible or hidden input exercises; compare patched output against the original code on generated inputs from the original's accepted input space.

symptom: wonder-1.0 solved 1 of 5 runs at effort=low; in the solved run attempt 3 received a concrete counterexample from the differential and fixed the patch; earlier 0/5 runs at effort=minimal (spark-1.3) got only a generic hidden-check failure message
root_cause: unknown; one possible factor is feedback concreteness, not isolated from model, effort, or chance
validity: n=1 recovery, different models and efforts across runs, single synthetic case; no controlled comparison
lesson: Do not claim that concrete counterexample feedback improves success until it is tested with the same model and effort and only the feedback varied.

symptom: with the differential removed as a gate (--no-differential), 5 patches were accepted on visible and hidden checks (spark-1.3 x2, wonder-1.0 x3); scored afterwards at differential seed 1, 4 of 5 diverged (core_divergences 60 each) and 1 passed
root_cause: same class as tn-001: patches rebuild the input handling by hand and fail on an empty record in the input; first listed examples in all 4 divergent runs are [[], ["t2","b"]] raising ValueError on both library versions
validity: synthetic case; effort=low; n=5 per model, one case; seed 1 yields 119 valid inputs vs 123 at seed 0 (overlap not measured); only the first 2 of 60 core divergences per run were listed; gate-on vs gate-off is not a controlled comparison
lesson: Visible and hidden checks accepted patches that a generated-input comparison against the original rejected; report differential-scored results next to accepted counts, and score with a seed that differs from the one used inside the loop.

symptom: 5 of 10 gate-off runs at effort=low (spark-1.3 x3, wonder-1.0 x2) reached max attempts; in all 15 attempts the hidden check failed on both library versions, while the visible check passed on both versions in 7 attempts and failed on both in 8
root_cause: not established for these 15 attempts; an earlier read patch (effort=minimal, spark-1.3, runs/20261027-190248 attempt 2) mapped "" and null to the same label "None" while the golden of the old library has "nan" for ""
validity: synthetic case; n=5 per model; patches of these attempts not read; failed runs used 89092 of 149148 tokens (about 60%) across the 10 runs
lesson: A failing hidden check on both versions means the patch does not preserve the old library behavior on inputs absent from the visible set; failed runs can carry most of the token cost, so report tokens for failed and accepted runs separately.

symptom: needed to know whether the Meta Model API accepts tools together with reasoning_effort and a full tool-result round trip
validity: one run per model (muse-wonder-1.0, muse-spark-1.3), reasoning_effort=low, one echo tool, two turns; tool_choice, parallel calls, longer conversations and content=None from the real API not tested
lesson: Both models returned tool_calls with valid JSON arguments and accepted the assistant message (with its extra refusal key) appended unchanged plus a role=tool message; reported prompt tokens grow per turn (493 to 576, 550 to 642), with part of the prompt reported as cached, so a tool loop re-sends and re-reports the context on every call.

symptom: patch rejected at the visible check on pandas 3: output has ["t1","nan",1] where the golden output has ["t1","None",1], although the patch contains a helper that maps None to "None"
root_cause: the patch left pd.DataFrame(records, columns=[...]) unchanged and normalized labels afterwards with .map(helper); under pandas 3 the DataFrame constructor already infers the new string dtype and turns None into NaN, so the helper never receives None and returns "nan"
validity: synthetic case; cause read from attempt_1.json and the attempt 3 diff, not re-run on pandas 3; one run (muse-wonder-1.0, effort=low, gate on)
lesson: Information lost at construction time cannot be restored by later normalization; fix the dtype at the point where the data enters the library (here dtype=object), then normalize. A correct-looking helper downstream is not evidence the fix works.

symptom: a patch that returns the golden output read from a golden file was accepted by the visible and hidden checks of the old gate in 6 of 6 cases and stopped only by the differential check
root_cause: the workspace copy used for checking held the whole case directory (golden, hidden golden, reference patches) and the expected output was read from that copy, so patched code could read it
validity: macOS, one cheat wrapper in two variants (relative path in the working directory, absolute path to the original case directory), 6 synthetic cases; variant A closes by removing the answer keys from the workspace and reading expected outputs from the original directory; variant B closes only with the OS layer
lesson: Keep answer keys out of any directory the candidate code runs in, read expected outputs from a location the candidate cannot reach, and write a negative test with a cheating candidate that must be rejected; run it against the old code first to show that it detects the leak.

symptom: under a macOS sandbox-exec profile that blocked file reads under the home directory and the repository and blocked the network, code inside the sandbox could still read the harness initial environment, where an API key held in an exported variable would be
root_cause: the environment of same-user processes is readable through a sysctl call; three extra Seatbelt rules and a default-deny profile did not block it in these tests; reading it through the ps command was blocked
validity: one macOS machine, fake secrets only, one run per probe; another same-user Python process was readable and a platform binary was not in one comparison; memory inspection tools and Linux were not tested
lesson: Do not rely on the profile to hide the harness environment: start the harness with a clean environment, keep the key in a 0600 file read at call time and never exported, refuse to run candidate code when secret-looking variables are in the initial environment, and test each protection with a positive control that shows the leak without the profile.

symptom: in a tool conversation with a 60000 token budget per run, the first attempt used 51527 tokens in 8 model calls and the second attempt was cut by the budget after 3 calls; the run total was 65834
root_cause: the context is re-sent on every model call (prompt tokens per call grew from 1409 to 8904, 78.6 percent of the attempt total, cached share not recorded) and the budget is checked only before a call, so one call can overshoot it; an attempt that ends on the budget right after a tool call never gets to write a final reply
validity: one run, muse-wonder-1.0, effort=low, synthetic case p4, smoke test; whether the second attempt could have finished without the cut was not tested
lesson: Size the per-run token budget for the cumulative context of a tool loop and not for one-shot calls, check it before each call with the size of the previous call in mind, and record how the final patch was submitted (final reply or last files passed to a tool).

symptom: with a run_probe tool that compares the original code on the old library with the candidate on the new library on inputs chosen by the model, 2 of 16 attempts failed the visible or hidden check and 8 of 16 passed both and failed the differential check; without tools 22 of 28 attempts failed visible or hidden and 3 of 28 the differential
root_cause: not established; one reading is that the model-driven oracle lets the model match the old behavior on inputs like the visible and hidden ones while generated inputs of other kinds still expose divergences; the patches of these attempts were not read
validity: muse-spark-1.3 and muse-wonder-1.0, effort=low, one synthetic case, n=5 runs per model and setting, different runs and different attempt counts (no tool run reached a third attempt), token budget 60000 per run, so the tool runs had about 1 to 2 attempts against 3 without tools
lesson: An oracle on inputs the model chooses itself does not replace an independent generated-input check; report the first failing gate per attempt next to accepted counts and the attempts per run, and size the budget so that a tool loop can use all its attempts before comparing it with a one-shot protocol.

symptom: two batches of the same command (muse-spark-1.3, effort=low, 5 runs per case on five cases, isolation layer on) both solved 25 of 25 runs but differed in first-try counts and token averages per case (for example p2_dst_day_offset average 3018 against 5139 tokens; one run of the second batch needed 3 attempts and 14172 tokens)
root_cause: run-to-run variation of the model at n=5 per case; not analyzed further
validity: one model for this comparison, one effort, five synthetic cases, two batches; wonder-1.0 had one batch (25 of 25 solved, 22 first try, average 2832 tokens)
lesson: Repeat an identical batch before reading a difference between two settings, and report solved, first-try and token counts together: the solved count alone was identical in the two batches and hid the variation.

symptom: the same 15-run command for p4, p1 and n7 was started twice, so two identical sweeps and a p7 batch shared one single-slot local server (-np 1) and overlapped in time; every run completed and every unsolved run ended with max attempts reached; the two sweeps solved p1 14 of 15 and 12 of 15, n7 5 of 15 and 3 of 15, p4 0 of 15 and 0 of 15
root_cause: a batch was launched without checking whether another batch was already using the server; there is no lock
validity: muse-glimmer Q4_K_M, reasoning strength low, counted rows, independent runs with the same configuration; wall-clock times are not usable; whether overlapping requests changed any result was not tested, only that none timed out as far as the recorded reasons show
lesson: Check for a running batch before starting one on a single-slot server and do not report times from overlapping batches. Two identical batches are a direct estimate of run-to-run spread: here 2 solved runs apart at n=15 on p1 and n7, which a 5-run table cannot show, so compare settings only with that spread in view.

symptom: two cases that each combine three independent silent breaks in one function (p8 pandas, n9 NumPy) were solved on the first attempt in 20 of 20 hosted runs (muse-spark-1.3 and muse-wonder-1.0, effort low, 5 runs per cell), while the local muse-glimmer solved p8 5 of 5 and n9 3 of 5
root_cause: not established; one reading is that the number of breaks matters less than whether a break hides behind a representation trap like the None versus NaN and value_counts order in p4, but the patches were not read and only one such case exists
validity: n=5 per cell, synthetic cases written by us, one model family, token counts only
lesson: Do not assume that stacking documented breaks makes a repair case harder; measure it and report the result either way. A case that separates models should be found by measurement, not by construction.

symptom: a repair case had to be built from an arbitrary user function without hand-written fixtures; the golden output and the held-out inputs must be trustworthy or the hidden and differential gates measure noise
root_cause: a generated input is only a valid held-out probe if the old library reproduces its output, so candidates from the differential generator are run twice on the old interpreter and kept only if both runs are equal and neither raises; among those, inputs where the new library differs are preferred so the hidden gate can reject a patch that restores only the visible inputs
validity: single hosted run per case (muse-spark-1.3, effort low): the n8 function rebuilt by the builder, first attempt, 3350 tokens, differential PASS with 133 valid inputs; scikit-FIBERS censor behind a thin adapter, first attempt, 2696 tokens, differential PASS with 144 valid inputs. censor is also the source of p7, so the breakage pattern is not new. Not tried: whole repositories, non-JSON arguments without an adapter, local Glimmer on these cases; local Muse Glimmer (effort low) on the censor case: 6 runs, 6 solved, 5 first try, 2167 to 4686 tokens, repeats of one case (per-run results copied from the terminal, not saved as a bench file). The two third-party cases and the recorded patches were later removed from the repository; what stays reproducible is gen2_test on the constructed o2 branch_on_version patch (generator 1: 21 valid probes, generator 2: 132, rejected)
lesson: Build the case generator so that it refuses instead of guessing: stop when the function raises on the old library, is not deterministic, fails loudly on the new library, or gives identical output. Verify the generated case with the same verdict function the agent uses (old OK, new SILENT_BREAKAGE, hidden old OK) before spending any model tokens.

symptom: two of five accepted patches branch on pd.__version__ (divide by 10**6 on pandas 3.0 and above) and are wrong for datetime64[ns] input; all gates passed because the differential returned WEAK with 10 valid probes (minimum 20)
root_cause: the input generator mutated the columns of a table independently (lists of different length are invalid for the DataFrame constructor in the wrapper) and mutated ISO date strings as text, so most probes raised on the old library and were discarded
validity: generator 2 (aligned lists, date-aware strings, 3/6/9 fractional digits) re-scored the 10 recorded patches without a model call: valid probes 29 to 157 (r1f) and 10 to 160 (r2f); both version-sniffing patches rejected, 3 unit-independent patches pass, one r1f patch rejected (8999.484757 vs 8999.484758). The generator was changed after seeing the failure, so this is not an independent test. The two third-party cases and the recorded patches were later removed from the repository; what stays reproducible is gen2_test on the constructed o2 branch_on_version patch (generator 1: 21 valid probes, generator 2: 132, rejected)
lesson: A property-based oracle is only as strong as the validity of its probes: count valid probes and report WEAK when few survive instead of passing. Generate inputs that respect structure (equal-length columns, parseable dates, several time resolutions) so most probes are valid, and keep the generator version in the case file so old results stay reproducible.

symptom: a fresh Linux clone could not run model code: the isolation layer depended on macOS sandbox-exec and the test runner required .venv
root_cause: platform-specific sandbox and a hard-coded interpreter path
validity: one Linux cloud VM (kernel 6.18.44, Landlock ABI 7), root and uid 1000: landlock_test 14 checks passed (fake secret, repository file, home listing and write, TCP to harness, /proc environ, symlink escape, signal, UDP with network namespace denied; workspace and pandas/numpy import allowed; control run with isolation off all allowed). UDP without the network namespace was allowed. Not tested: other kernels, seccomp-restricted containers, a model run on Linux
lesson: On Linux use Landlock through ctypes (syscalls 444 to 446, no libraries, no privileges) as an allow list: mask the access rights by the ABI the kernel reports, add TCP rules from ABI 4 and signal scope from ABI 6, add an empty user+net namespace for UDP, and exit non-zero when Landlock is missing so nothing runs unisolated. Every isolation test needs a control run with the isolation off, and secrets must be given as explicit absolute paths, otherwise a test can pass vacuously.

symptom: benchmark cases built from other projects' functions require licenses, notices and adapters, and make the repository depend on code we do not control
root_cause: copying real functions was the way to show the breakage is real, but the same evidence can be kept as a search log while the code under repair is written by us from the documented mechanism
validity: three own cases (two datetime-resolution, one chained assignment) all VALID; muse-glimmer local 45/45 solved (44 first try), muse-spark-1.3 15/15 and muse-wonder-1.0 15/15 solved on the first try, all re-scored PASS; the cases are easy and do not separate the models
lesson: Write the function under repair yourself from the documented change, put the held-out inputs and the known-bad patches next to it, and keep real-project evidence as a protocol plus a search log. Include one constructed bad patch that passes plain inputs but fails on unusual ones (here a pandas version branch) to show that the oracle can reject it.

symptom: on o1 to o3 every model solved every run at the first attempt, so the benchmark did not show what the hidden gate is for
root_cause: the visible inputs contained everything needed to find the fix; a partial or version-specific patch was never penalised
validity: three cases whose visible inputs allow an incomplete fix (alias writes where only one is exercised, epoch seconds without gaps or offsets, scalar repr with float columns only), held-out inputs written by hand: 29 of 75 first-pass attempts passed the visible check and failed the hidden check (muse-glimmer local 27, muse-wonder 2, muse-spark 0); Glimmer solved 42 of 45 (27 first try), hosted models 30 of 30; counts per attempt from local files; one batch per model and case
lesson: To measure a verification gate, build cases where the cheap fix is plausible: give the visible inputs a narrow slice of the behavior and keep the missing slice (gaps, offsets, other dtypes, the second broken site) in held-out inputs, and add a known-bad patch for each cheap fix so the case proves the gate rejects it before any model runs. Report rejected-at-gate counts, not only solved counts.

symptom: the repair command works on one function at a time; a real code base has many functions, most of them unaffected by an upgrade, and a few that fail loudly rather than silently
root_cause: a repair loop has no way to know which functions need repair unless it first compares old and new behavior; running the model on every function wastes tokens and risks rewriting code that is fine
validity: eight functions we wrote (five silent breaks, two unaffected, one raising AttributeError on NumPy 2), one run with local muse-glimmer (effort low): triage classified all eight correctly; four of five silent breaks were repaired at the first attempt (1049, 896, 1007 and 936 tokens), the fifth (float32 times a Python float, where the old behavior is float64) was not repaired in three attempts (3924 tokens) because the model forced float32 on both libraries; the gates rejected all three and no file changed; 183 s and 7812 tokens for the whole command; one run, not a rate
lesson: Triage before repair: run every function with its inputs on both library versions, repair only the ones whose output differs without an exception, and report the others without touching them. A function that raises on the new library is a loud failure and needs no silent-break machinery. When the model misreads the direction of a behavior change, the gates still refuse the patch; report that outcome as it is.
